# Round-trip fixture provenance and truth contract

The three screenplay families in this directory are maintained interoperability
fixtures. Their human-authored `.fountain` files are the semantic source of
truth; the companion `.fdx` and `.pdf` files exercise other input boundaries.
`contracts.json` contains a deliberately reviewed, non-generated set of identity,
ordered-scene, speaker, and dialogue anchors. The tests additionally compare the
complete ordered heading sequence and require every renderable source token to
survive conversion.

The previous `*-golden.json` files were generated by
`extract_golden_metadata.py`. That heuristic mislabeled action, transitions,
sections, and title markup as characters, and its counts could be regenerated
from the same source without review. Both the generated files and generator were
removed in the July 2026 truth audit. They are not valid golden references.

## Recorded provenance

All nine format fixtures entered the repository together in git commit
`ff7792a` on 2026-02-22 (`Standardize screenplay format round-trip and
high-fidelity rendering (Story 064)`). Story 064 says they were copied from the
local directory `input/Perfect Script Samples/` and explicitly identifies the
Fountain files as human-authored ground truth. Neither that story nor the git
history records an upstream URL, download date, checksum at acquisition, or the
person who performed an external-content review. The exact download origins are
therefore unknown; this file does not infer them.

Fixture-embedded credits and notices provide the identity evidence that can be
verified locally:

- **Big Fish**: title `Big Fish`; `written by John August`; based on the novel by
  Daniel Wallace; marked `FINAL PRODUCTION DRAFT`; copyright notice `(c) 2003
  Columbia Pictures`.
- **Brick & Steel: Full Retired**: title `BRICK & STEEL / FULL RETIRED`;
  `Written by Stu Maschwitz`; `Story by KTM`; draft date `1/27/2012`; a Next
  Level Productions contact block. No copyright notice is embedded.
- **The Last Birthday Card**: title `THE LAST BIRTHDAY CARD`; `Written by Stu
  Maschwitz`; draft date `7/8/1998`; contact block and `Registered WGAw No.
  701428`. No copyright notice is embedded.

The companion Last Birthday Card PDF contains three source-visible historical
spelling divergences: `APPARTMENT` for `APARTMENT` (twice), `THREATTM` for
`THREAT`, and `DEDUCTABLE` for `DEDUCTIBLE`. The explicit aliases in
`contracts.json` apply only when binding that committed PDF back to its Fountain
source. They are not applied to newly generated output.

## Fidelity policy

- Every complete scene-heading token sequence must survive in screenplay order,
  and the extracted heading count must be exact. Token comparison intentionally
  tolerates smart quotes, spaces around dashes, and PDF line wrapping; there is
  no count tolerance and no set-only comparison.
- Reviewed dialogue anchors bind a standalone character cue to nearby exact
  dialogue and are checked in screenplay order.
- Fountain-to-PDF extraction must retain every renderable source token. PDF
  page numbers, `(CONT'D)`, and `(MORE)` can add tokens, so output-only tokens
  are allowed only while source-token precision remains at least 99%. The July
  2026 baseline measured 99.39% to 99.57% precision across the three fixtures.
- The committed source PDFs must retain every Fountain token after only the
  explicitly reviewed spelling aliases above. `&`/`AND`, `(c)`/`©`, smart
  quotes, and whitespace are normalized as typography, not content loss. Their
  measured source-token precision is 99.44% (Big Fish), 98.72% (Brick & Steel),
  and 99.28% (The Last Birthday Card); the per-fixture floors in
  `contracts.json` sit just below those observed values because the committed
  PDFs add page numbers and continuation cues.
- Output-only token values are also restricted by fixture. Numeric additions
  must be plausible page numbers bounded by the actual PDF page count;
  `(MORE)`, `(CONT'D)`, and listed speaker-name additions are likewise bounded
  by that count. Big Fish additionally repeats the visible `Copyright`
  title-page label. Arbitrary words, implausible numbers, and overproduced
  pagination tokens fail even when the precision floor would otherwise pass.
- A visual dual-dialogue row must reflow into two ordered speaker/dialogue
  blocks, with the second cue retaining Fountain's `^` marker. The stricter
  ordered-token check exposed and now guards the prior `STEEL BRICK` merged-cue
  failure in the Brick & Steel PDF.
- PDF-to-Fountain-to-PDF must reopen and extract the newly rendered PDF. Every
  token extracted from the original PDF must remain an ordered subsequence of
  the second extraction; only renderer-added pagination markers may intervene.
